It defines a clear partnership vision that articulates the purpose, desired outcomes, and guiding principles for collaboration with external partners.
This process defines the strategic assumptions, constraints, and opportunities that shape partnership vision, objectives, and principles by considering enterprise priorities, market dynamics, supply chain requirements, competitive positioning, and Business Partner Environment trends.
It formulates partnership objectives and value propositions that clarify how partnerships contribute to value creation, innovation, resilience, and market positioning, without identifying or selecting specific partners.
The outcome is a coherent and well-defined partner strategy that serves as a stable reference for subsequent classification, governance, portfolio planning, and lifecycle management.

name: Define Partnerships Strategic Context
brief_description: Define Partnerships Strategic Context defines the strategic assumptions, constraints, and opportunities shaping the business partner strategy, considering enterprise priorities, market dynamics, supply chain context, and Business Partner Environment conditions
extended_description:
Define Partnerships Strategic Context process defines the strategic assumptions, constraints, and opportunities that shape the organizations approach to business partnerships within the Business Partner Environment and broader value chain.
It establishes a shared understanding of internal and external factors influencing the role, scope, and direction of partnerships, including enterprise strategy, business priorities, market dynamics, regulatory considerations, and supply chain context.
This process analyzes relevant market, competitive, technological, and industry developments to identify opportunities and constraints that partnerships are expected to address or leverage. It also considers organizational capabilities, strategic ambitions, and boundary conditions that frame how partnerships support value creation, innovation, and market positioning.

name: Define Partnership Vision
brief_description: Define Partnership Vision defines the long-term vision for business partnerships across the enterprise value chain, including supply chain articulating their purpose, ambition, and strategic role in achieving enterprise objectives.
extended_description:
Define Partnership Vision process defines the long-term vision for business partnerships across the enterprises value chain, including supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships within the Business Partner Environment. It articulates the purpose, ambition, and intended role of partnerships in supporting the organizations enterprise objectives.
This process establishes how partnerships are expected to contribute to value creation, innovation, market positioning, operational resilience, and sustainable growth, in alignment with corporate strategy and brand values. It defines the desired future state of the Business Partner Environment and clarifies the strategic role partnerships play within the organizations broader business and operating model.
The process provides a unifying strategic narrative that explains why the organization engages with partners, what outcomes partnerships are intended to enable, and how partnership success is conceptually defined at a strategic level. It serves as a reference for shaping partnership objectives, value propositions, classification strategies, and governance direction.

name: Define Partnership Objectives
brief_description: Define Partnership Objectives defines the strategic objectives for business partnerships across the enterprise value chain, translating the partnership vision into  measurable outcomes aligned with enterprise priorities.
extended_description:
Define Partnership Objectives process defines the strategic objectives that translate the partnership vision into specific, measurable outcomes for business partnerships across the enterprises value chain, including supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships within the Business Partner Environment.
This process establishes short- and long-term objectives that clarify what the organization seeks to achieve through partnerships, such as growth, innovation, market access, capability enhancement, operational resilience, supply chain performance, and customer value creation. It ensures that partnership objectives are aligned with enterprise strategy, measurable through appropriate indicators, and realistic within strategic constraints and market conditions.
The process defines objectives at a strategic level without identifying specific partners or defining operational targets.

name: Define Partnership Value Propositions
brief_description: Define Partnership Value Propositions defines the strategic value propositions for business partnerships across the enterprise value chain, articulating how mutual value is created in support of enterprise objectives and the partnership vision.
extended_description:
Define Partnership Value Propositions process defines the strategic value propositions that articulate how business partnerships across the enterprises value chain—including supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships within the Business Partner Environment—are intended to create mutual value for the organization and its partners in alignment with enterprise objectives and the partnership vision.
This process defines the types of value that partnerships are expected to deliver, such as innovation enablement, market access, capability extension, operational efficiency, supply chain resilience, differentiation, or brand enhancement. It establishes the value logic that underpins the partner strategy by clarifying what the organization seeks to gain from partnerships and the value it intends to offer in return.

name: Define Partnerships Principles
brief_description: Define Partnerships Principles defines the guiding principles that frame how business partnerships across the enterprise value chain are established, governed, and evolved in alignment with the partnership vision and enterprise strategy.
extended_description:
Define Partnership Principles process defines the set of guiding principles that shape the organizations approach to business partnerships across the enterprises value chain, including supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships within the Business Partner Environment. These principles provide strategic direction for how partnerships are established, governed, and sustained over time.
The process articulates the values, behaviors, and expectations that underpin collaboration with partners, ensuring consistency with enterprise strategy, brand values, and risk posture. It defines principles such as transparency, accountability, value sharing, trust, compliance, sustainability, and responsible collaboration.
These principles guide partnership decision-making across the Business Partner Environment without defining operational rules, governance mechanisms, or partner-specific obligations. They serve as strategic guardrails that inform partner classification, governance strategy, portfolio planning, and partnership lifecycle management.

name: Define Partner Classification Strategy
brief_description: Define Partner Classification Strategy defines the strategic framework for structuring and classifying partners ecosystem by establishing partner types, classification principles, and classification-level intent to guide portfolio planning, capability dev
extended_description:
Define Partner Classification Strategy process defines the strategic framework for structuring and classifying the organizations Business Partner Environment, including supply chain, commercial, and innovation partners. It defines partner types, classification dimensions, and participation principles that describe how different partner categories contribute to value creation, innovation, market reach, and operational enablement.
This process defines the purpose, scope, and expected contribution of each partner classification, including eligibility principles, collaboration intent, participation expectations, strategic commitment, enablement depth, and governance intensity, including supply chain relationships, without assessing or selecting individual partners.
The resulting classification model provides a consistent reference that supports portfolio planning, capability development, governance design, and lifecycle management.

name: Define Partner Classification Objectives
brief_description: Define Partner Classification Objectives defines the strategic objectives that partner classification is expected to support across the Business Partner Environment, guiding how partners are grouped and differentiated.
extended_description:
Define Partner Classification Objectives process defines the strategic objectives that the partner classification strategy is expected to support across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
Define Partner Classification Dimensions process defines the strategic dimensions and criteria used to classify partners across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships. These dimensions provide the structural basis for consistently differentiating partner types according to their intended strategic role and value contribution.
This process identifies the key classification dimensions used to distinguish partners, such as strategic role, value contribution, collaboration scope, position within the value chain, market focus, or innovation involvement. These dimensions reflect how partners contribute to enterprise objectives rather than how they perform operationally.
The classification dimensions are defined at a strategic level and do not rely on operational performance metrics or capability assessments. They ensure clarity, consistency, and alignment with partnership objectives, value propositions, and enterprise strategy.

name: Define Partner Classification Dimensions
brief_description: Define Partner Classification Dimensions defines the strategic dimensions and criteria used to classify partners across the Business Partner Environment based on strategic roles and value logic.
extended_description:
Define Partner Classification Dimensions process defines the strategic dimensions and criteria used to classify partners across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships. These dimensions provide the structural basis for consistently differentiating partner types according to their intended strategic role and value contribution.
This process identifies the key classification dimensions used to distinguish partners, such as strategic role, value contribution, collaboration scope, position within the value chain, market focus, or innovation involvement. These dimensions reflect how partners contribute to enterprise objectives rather than how they perform operationally.
The classification dimensions are defined at a strategic level and do not rely on operational performance metrics or capability assessments. They ensure clarity, consistency, and alignment with partnership objectives, value propositions, and enterprise strategy.

name: Define Partner Types
brief_description: Define Partner Types defines the standard partner types across the Business Partner Environment, translating classification objectives and dimensions into distinct strategic partner categories.
extended_description:
Define Partner Types process defines the standard partner types across the Business Partner Environment, at a conceptual level, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships. These partner types represent distinct strategic categories, each associated with a specific role and intended contribution to enterprise objectives.
This process translates partner classification objectives and dimensions into clearly defined partner types by combining the relevant classification criteria into meaningful and consistent categories. Each partner type reflects a distinct strategic role, value contribution, collaboration scope, or position within the value chain.
Partner types describe how different categories of partners are expected to support value creation, innovation, market reach, operational enablement, and supply chain performance.
The resulting set of partner types provides a common reference framework that supports consistent communication, portfolio planning, governance strategy, and partnership lifecycle management across the organization.

name: Define Partner Participation Principles
brief_description: Define Partner Participation Principles defines the high-level participation and collaboration intent, and eligibility principles applicable to each partner type across the Business Partner Environment.
extended_description:
Define Partner Participation Principles process defines the high-level principles that govern how different partner types are intended to participate in the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships. It establishes the strategic participation and collaboration intent applicable to each partner type.
This process defines eligibility principles and high-level participation expectations that clarify how different partner types are expected to engage with the organization based on their strategic role, value contribution, and position within the value chain. It describes the intended nature, scope, and depth of collaboration without defining operational interaction models, governance mechanisms, or partner-specific arrangements.
Participation principles ensure that collaboration expectations are consistent with partner strategy, enterprise values, and risk appetite, while enabling coherent and differentiated engagement approaches across partner types.

name:
Define Partner
Strategic Commitment
brief_description:
Define Partner
Strategic Commitment defines the level of strategic commitment and organizational support the organization intends to provide to each partner type across the Business Partner Environment.
extended_description:
Define Partner Strategic Commitment process defines the level of strategic commitment and organizational support that the organization intends to provide to each partner type across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
This process establishes how strongly the organization intends to engage with different partner types based on their strategic role, expected value contribution, and importance to enterprise objectives. It clarifies the relative level of commitment associated with each partner type, including the degree of strategic focus, enablement support, collaboration intensity, and long-term engagement intent.
Strategic commitment reflects the organizations intended level of prioritization and support for each partner type, complementing participation principles that define how partners engage. It ensures that different partner types are supported in a manner consistent with their strategic importance and role within the value chain.
These commitments are defined at a strategic level and are not expressed as financial investments, operational programs, or partner-specific arrangements.
The resulting commitment framework provides a consistent reference for guiding partner enablement strategies, resource prioritization, governance design, and partnership lifecycle management.

name: Define Partner Governance Strategy
brief_description: Define Partner Governance Strategy process defines the strategic principles, oversight posture, and governance intent that guide how business partnerships are governed across the Business Partner Environment.
extended_description:
Define Partner Governance Strategy process defines the strategic principles, oversight posture, and governance intent that guide how business partnerships are governed across the Business Partner Environment, including supply chain relationships. It establishes how partnerships are directed, controlled, and aligned with enterprise strategy, partnership vision, and organizational values.
This process defines governance direction across partner types, including accountability principles, decision authority, escalation approach, compliance expectations, risk oversight, and performance stewardship at a strategic level. It ensures consistent governance across different categories of partners without defining operational governance mechanisms or partner-specific controls.
The process provides a strategic reference for governance frameworks, operating models, and lifecycle controls, enabling coherent and scalable governance of all partnerships across the enterprise value chain.

name: Define Partner Governance Intent
brief_description: Define Partner Governance Intent defines the strategic intent that guides how business partnerships are governed across the Business Partner Environment and enterprise value chain in alignment with enterprise strategy and partnership objectives.
extended_description:
Define Partner Governance Intent process defines the strategic intent that frames how business partnerships are to be governed across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
It clarifies the role governance is expected to play in directing, overseeing, and safeguarding partnerships to ensure alignment with enterprise strategy, partnership vision, and organizational values. This includes defining the intended purpose of governance in supporting value creation, ensuring accountability, managing risk exposure, and enabling sustainable collaboration.
The process articulates expectations for responsible oversight, alignment with enterprise priorities, protection of organizational interests, and support for long-term partnership effectiveness.
The governance intent is defined at a strategic level and does not specify governance structures, operational mechanisms, decision workflows, or partner-specific controls.

name: Define Partner Governance Principles
brief_description: Define Partner Governance Principles defines the guiding principles that frame how business partnerships are governed and overseen across the Business Partner Environment and enterprise value chain.
extended_description:
The Define Partner Governance Principles process defines the set of guiding principles that shape how governance is applied to business partnerships across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
These principles translate the governance intent into a coherent set of foundational rules and expectations that guide how partnerships are directed and overseen in alignment with enterprise strategy, partnership objectives, and organizational values.
The process articulates governance principles such as transparency, accountability, consistency, proportional oversight, regulatory compliance, and responsible collaboration. These principles define how governance should be applied at a strategic level and guide the design and operation of governance structures and decision-making approaches.
The resulting set of governance principles provides a consistent reference that informs decision authority, risk oversight, performance oversight, and governance framework design.

name: Define Partner Decision Authority
brief_description: Define Partner Decision Authority defines the strategic intent for how decision authority and accountability are distributed for business partnerships across the Business Partner Environment and enterprise value chain.
extended_description:
Define Partner Decision Authority process defines the strategic intent for how decision authority and accountability are to be distributed within the governance of business partnerships across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
It establishes the high-level direction for how decisions affecting partnerships should be authorized, escalated, and overseen, based on governance principles and in alignment with enterprise strategy and partnership objectives. This includes defining the governance perspective on decision boundaries, levels of authority, and accountability expectations for strategic partnership decisions.
The process clarifies how responsibility for decisions such as partnership direction, approval of partnership initiatives, and escalation of significant partnership matters should be structured at a strategic level, without assigning operational roles, defining governance structures, or specifying decision-making workflows.
Decision authority ensures that governance supports accountability, transparency, and alignment with enterprise priorities, while enabling consistent and effective oversight across all partner types.

name: Define Partner Risk Oversight Approach
brief_description: Define Partner Risk Oversight Approach defines the strategic approach for governing and overseeing partnership-related risks across the Business Partner Environment and enterprise value chain, in alignment with enterprise risk management practices.
extended_description:
The Define Partner Risk Oversight Approach process defines the strategic approach for governing and overseeing risks associated with business partnerships across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
It establishes how governance should address risks arising from collaboration with partners while ensuring alignment with enterprise risk management practices, policies, and risk tolerance. This includes defining the governance perspective on how partnership-related risks are to be monitored, escalated, and supervised at a strategic level.
The process clarifies the scope and nature of risks relevant to partnerships, including strategic, operational, regulatory, reputational, and technology risks that may arise across the partner landscape.

name: Define Partner Performance Oversight Approach
brief_description: Define Partner Performance Oversight Approach defines the strategic approach for governing and overseeing partnership performance across the Business Partner Environment and enterprise value chain.
extended_description:
Define Partner Performance Oversight Approach process defines the strategic approach for governing and overseeing the performance of business partnerships across the Business Partner Environment, including partnerships across the enterprise value chain such as supply chain, commercial, and innovation relationships.
It establishes how governance should ensure that partnerships deliver intended value and remain aligned with partnership objectives and enterprise priorities. This includes defining the governance perspective on how partnership outcomes are to be monitored, reviewed, and supervised at a strategic level.
The process clarifies expectations for oversight of partnership performance, including stewardship of outcomes, accountability for achieving strategic objectives, and alignment with value creation goals across different partner types and roles within the value chain.
This process defines the principles and direction that guide how partnership performance should be observed and evaluated at a governance level.

name: Optimize Partner Strategy
brief_description: Optimize Partner Strategy continuously reviews and refines the partner strategy to maintain alignment with enterprise objectives, Business Partner Environment evolution, and supply chain priorities.
extended_description:
Optimize Partner Strategy process periodically reviews and refines the organizations partner strategy to ensure continued alignment with enterprise objectives, evolving Business Partner Environment conditions, and supply chain requirements. It evaluates the relevance, coherence, and effectiveness of partnership vision, objectives, classification strategy, and governance direction.
This process assesses insights derived from business performance, partnership outcomes, market dynamics, supply chain evolution, competitive pressures, and regulatory developments to identify necessary adjustments. It focuses on refining strategic priorities, assumptions, and guiding principles without engaging in partner-specific decisions.
The process ensures that the partner strategy remains current, resilient, and aligned with enterprise priorities while supporting continuous strategic alignment across all partnership types.

name: Assess Partner Strategy Effectiveness
brief_description: Assess Partner Strategy Effectiveness evaluates the effectiveness and continued relevance of the partner strategy in supporting enterprise objectives and value creation across the Business Partner Environment and value chain.
extended_description:
Assess Partner Strategy Effectiveness process evaluates the effectiveness and continued relevance of the organizations partner strategy in achieving enterprise objectives and delivering intended partnership outcomes across the Business Partner Environment and the broader enterprise value chain, including supply chain relationships.
It reviews how well the current partnership vision, strategic objectives, classification strategy, and governance direction contribute to value creation, innovation, market reach, and operational enablement across different partner roles and value chain segments.
This process analyzes strategic insights derived from business performance trends, partnership outcomes, and broader strategic indicators to determine whether the partner strategy remains coherent, effective, and aligned with evolving enterprise priorities and external conditions.
The assessment focuses on strategic-level evaluation rather than operational partner performance, partner-specific assessments, or execution effectiveness.
The outcome of this process is a set of strategic insights that inform potential adjustments to partnership vision, objectives, classification, and governance direction, supporting continuous alignment of the partner strategy with enterprise goals.

name: Assess Business Partner Environment Changes
brief_description: Assess Business Partner Environment Changes evaluates external changes in the Business Partner Environment and value chain that may impact the relevance, assumptions, or direction of the partner strategy.
extended_description:
Assess Business Partner Environment Changes process evaluates developments and shifts within the Business Partner Environment and the broader enterprise value chain, including supply chain dynamics, that may influence the direction, assumptions, or effectiveness of the organizations partner strategy.
It considers external and contextual factors such as market dynamics, technological evolution, competitive developments, regulatory changes, ecosystem restructuring, and industry trends that affect partnership opportunities, collaboration models, and value chain configurations.
This process analyzes how these environmental changes may impact the strategic roles of partners, the relevance of existing partner classification structures, and the suitability of governance approaches. It focuses on interpreting external signals and structural shifts in the Business Partner Environment rather than assessing internal strategy performance or evaluating specific partners.
The process provides forward-looking strategic insight into how the evolving environment may affect partnership priorities, strategic positioning, and collaboration models, supporting proactive adaptation of the partner strategy.

name: Identify Partner Strategy Adjustment Needs
brief_description: Identify Partner Strategy Adjustment Needs identifies and prioritizes required adjustments to the partner strategy based on insights from strategy effectiveness assessments and changes in the Business Partner Environment and value chain.
extended_description:
Identify Partner Strategy Adjustment Needs process determines whether and where adjustments to the partner strategy are required based on insights from strategy effectiveness assessments and analysis of changes within the Business Partner Environment and the broader enterprise value chain, including supply chain dynamics.
It evaluates potential gaps, misalignments, and emerging opportunities that may require modification of strategic assumptions, priorities, guiding principles, or structural elements of the partner strategy. This includes assessing whether current partnership objectives, classification strategy, governance direction, and strategic focus areas remain aligned with enterprise priorities and evolving business conditions.
This process synthesizes internal (strategy effectiveness) and external (environmental change) insights to identify and articulate clear strategic adjustment needs. It focuses on defining what needs to change and why, without yet refining or redesigning the strategy.
The outcome of this process is a structured set of prioritized strategic adjustment needs that provide direction for subsequent refinement of the partner strategy, ensuring continued alignment with enterprise objectives and the evolving Business Partner Environment.

name: Refine Partner Strategy Direction
brief_description: Refine Partner Strategy Direction refines and updates the partner strategy based on identified adjustment needs to maintain alignment with enterprise priorities and the evolving Business Partner Environment and value chain.
extended_description:
The Refine Partner Strategy Direction process updates and refines the overall strategic direction of the partner strategy based on identified adjustment needs. It revisits and adjusts strategic assumptions, priorities, guiding principles, and strategic focus areas to ensure continued alignment with enterprise objectives and the evolving Business Partner Environment and broader value chain, including supply chain dynamics.
This process translates identified strategic adjustment needs into concrete updates to the partner strategy. It may refine elements such as the partnership vision, strategic objectives, partner classification strategy, and governance direction at a strategic level.
The refinement focuses on evolving the strategic framework that guides partnerships rather than modifying operational partnership activities, partner relationships, or execution mechanisms. It ensures that strategic changes are coherent, consistent, and aligned across all elements of the partner strategy.
The outcome of this process is an updated and aligned partner strategy that reflects current enterprise priorities and environmental conditions, providing a clear and actionable strategic direction for subsequent planning, governance, and partnership lifecycle management.

name: Validate Updated Partner Strategy Alignment
brief_description: Validate Updated Partner Strategy Alignment validates that the updated partner strategy is coherent and aligned with enterprise strategy, governance direction, and the evolving Business Partner Environment and value chain.
extended_description:
Validate Updated Partner Strategy Alignment process confirms that the updated partner strategy remains fully aligned with enterprise strategy, organizational priorities, governance direction, and the evolving Business Partner Environment and broader value chain, including supply chain dynamics.
It ensures that adjustments to the partner strategy maintain coherence across all strategic elements, including partnership vision, strategic objectives, partner classification strategy, and governance principles. The process verifies that these elements are consistently aligned with enterprise priorities, strategic commitments, and the organizations overall approach to collaboration.
This process performs a strategic-level validation of the updated direction to ensure internal consistency, completeness, and alignment, without redefining strategy elements or reassessing environmental or performance factors.
The outcome of this process is validated assurance that the updated partner strategy is coherent, aligned, and ready to guide subsequent planning, governance implementation, and partnership lifecycle activities, supporting sustainable collaboration and long-term value creation.

name: Business Partner Tender Management
brief_description: Business Partner Tender Management processes manage the activities associated with developing tender documents, running tender processes, gaining enterprise agreement to tender decisions.
extended_description:
Business Partner Tender Management processes manage the activities associated with developing tender documents, running tender processes, gaining enterprise agreement to tender decisions.
The tender process for the sourcing activity can be used not only for managing the sourcing of infrastructure of various types, but is also applicable for use in outsourcing tender processes, and for the sourcing of commodity items used within a business. The actual depth to which the sourcing process is used is dependent on such factors as the value of the sourced items. Note that these processes can also be used for the negotiated agreements between the enterprise and its competitors as a part of regulated inter-carrier agreements. While tender processes are not used in such a case, the processes for determining appropriate commercial arrangements and for gaining enterprise agreement are used for these regulated and competitive activities.
They also manage the evaluation of agreements with parties, to determine those with the products and services that best meet the enterprise’s needs.

name: Determine the Sourcing Requirements
brief_description: Manage the collection and finalization of the specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process.
extended_description:
The Determine the Sourcing Requirements processes manage the collection and finalization of the specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process including a chronological timetable for anticipated sourcing activities. These requirements take into account the required functional, technical and/or operational specifications produced by the area seeking the sourcing activity and assuring that appropriately aligned commercial aspects (such as special commercial terms, tender timing, cost parameters, etc.) are catered for. The requirements will be determined from the requirements specified in the various business or investment proposals, and any subsequent detailed specifications developed as a part of the architecture design activity, within the product, market, service or resource capability delivery processes. The actual range of requirements are dependent on the needs of the sourcing initiator, but are likely to include, at a minimum, technical, operational, training and specific supplier support requirements.
The Party Strategy and Planning processes will also provide a set of enterprise level requirements that the sourcing process will need to satisfy.
The processes include any interaction with cross-enterprise coordination and management functions to ensure that the requirements meets the needs of all stakeholders

name: Capture Sourcing Requirements
brief_description: These processes manage the collection of the specific requirements and timetable to be achieved from the sourcing process. These requirements take into account the required functional, technical and/or operational specifications produced by the area seeking the sourcing activity and assuring that appropriately aligned commercial aspects (such as special commercial terms, tender timing, cost parameters, etc.) are catered for.
extended_description:
These processes manage the collection of the specific requirements and timetable to be achieved from the sourcing process. These requirements take into account the required functional, technical and/or operational specifications produced by the area seeking the sourcing activity and assuring that appropriately aligned commercial aspects (such as special commercial terms, tender timing, cost parameters, etc.) are catered for. The requirements will be determined from the requirements specified in the various business or investment proposals, and any subsequent detailed specifications developed as a part of the architecture design activity, within the product, market, service or resource capability delivery processes. The actual range of requirements are dependent on the needs of the sourcing initiator, but are likely to include, at a minimum, technical, operational, training and specific supplier support requirements. Detailed analysis of new resource requirements linked to relevant geographic distributions. These processes also establish the detailed performance requirements....much of the following about demand and capacity is performed by P/S/R Capability Delivery processes...so it should reference them rather than duplicating the tasks performed by them... These processes take the forecast information available from the Produce Resource Business Plans and requirements information from the Map & Analyze Service Requirements processes, as well as resource infrastructure requirements developed by the Develop Detailed Resource Specifications processes, to establish detailed views of anticipated resource demand and performance requirements.
These processes manage the capacity planning for the resource infrastructure, and identify capacity requirements based on service forecasts and appropriate resource related metrics, i.e., transaction volumes, storage requirements, traffic volumes, port availabilities, etc. The Party Strategy and Planning processes will also provide a set of enterprise level requirements that the sourcing process will need to satisfy.

name: Finalize Sourcing Requirements
brief_description: These processes manage the finalization of the specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process including a chronological timetable for anticipated sourcing activities.
extended_description: These processes manage the finalization of the specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process including a chronological timetable for anticipated sourcing activities. The processes include any interaction with cross-enterprise coordination and management functions to ensure that the ...what is demand distribution?...demand distributions capture the needs of all stakeholders.

name: Prepare Tender Document
brief_description: Develop a formal tender document that contains specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process created by the Finalize Sourcing Requirements process.
extended_description:
Prepare Tender Document develops a formal tender document that contains specific requirements to be achieved from the sourcing process created by the Finalize Sourcing Requirements process.

The tender document may be in the form of a request for proposal (RFP), request for information (RFI), or a request for quotation (RFQ). Once prepared it is issued to potential parties as part of the Determine Potential Parties process.

name: Determine Potential Parties
brief_description: Determine the appropriate short list of parties to meet the specific enterprise requirements.
extended_description:
The Determine Potential Parties processes determine the appropriate short list of parties to meet the specific enterprise requirements (for example, expected technical capability, anticipated delivery timeframes, anticipated costs, etc..). The processes provide detailed analysis of potential parties, leveraging information available from the Gather & Analyze Value Fabric Information
The processes include any interaction with cross-enterprise coordination and management functions to ensure that the selected short list meets the needs of all stakeholders

name: Analyze Potential Parties
brief_description: Analyze potential parties using available internal and external information to assess suitability.
extended_description: These processes provide detailed analysis of potential parties, leveraging information available from the Gather & Analyze Value Fabric Information processes...need to align this with the final name of this process - it was Supply Chain instead of VF, as well as other specific inputs available from within the enterprise, or from external party research organizations at the specific time the need arises.

name: Short List Potential Parties
brief_description: Select a shortlist of potential parties that meet enterprise requirements.
extended_description: These processes specify the appropriate short list of parties, based on the available analysis of potential parties, to meet the specific enterprise requirements (for example, expected technical capability, anticipated delivery timeframes, anticipated costs, etc..).

name: Identify Potential Parties
brief_description: Identify potential parties who may engage with the enterprise.
extended_description:
Identify  Potential  Parties identifies potential parties who may engage with the enterprise. Their identification is based on, but not limited to information gathered by the Party Strategy & Planning process and other research performed as part of this process.

In some cases a nondisclosure agreement may be required with a potential party that would trigger the Party Agreement Management process.  For example the exchange of catalogs may require such an agreement.

name: Issue Tender Document
brief_description: Issue the prepared tender document to selected parties.

name: Receive Tender Document Response
brief_description: Receive tender document response from a identified party to whom the tender document was sent.
extended_description: Receive Tender Document Response accepts a tender document response from a party to whom the tender document was sent. The response is used by the Selected Short-listed Party process which selects on or more parties with whom agreements are negotiated.

name: Select Short-listed Business Partner
brief_description: Select a Business Partner with whom an agreement is to be negotiated.
extended_description:
Select Short-listed Business Partner select a Business Partner with whom an agreement is to be negotiated.

The Business Partner may be selected based on their response to a formal tender document that was issued or only based on the results of using requirements gathered by the applicable Determine Sourcing Requirements sub-processes and the other Determine Potential Parties sub-processes.

This process typically involves some form of interaction with a short-listed Business Partner, such as a visit to the Business Partner's site(s), a visit to the enterprise site(s) , conference calls, and so forth.  The interaction should include one or more demonstrations of the Business Partner's capability to satisfy requirements.

This process may be repeated if more than one Business Partner is selected from the short list of parties.

name: Manage the Tender Process
brief_description: Manage and administer the mechanics of the tender process.
extended_description:
The Manage the Tender Process processes  manage and administer the mechanics of the tender process. The processes determine the engagement interactions with potential parties, the timing of the process, bring together the commercial and functional requirements into the tender documentation, the analysis and scoring mechanisms for tender analysis based on the functional, technical, operational and commercial requirements, and manage the tender analysis team engagement approach.
These processes are invoked by the Party Order Handling processes in the event that the order process requires a tender to select between previously contracted parties.
These processes also manage the analysis of the strategic sourcing factors used at the commencement of the process including the industry and competitive analysis, and a determination of the minimum acceptable outcomes from the sourcing process.

name: Specify the Tender Process
brief_description: Define the tender process, including requirements, timing, engagement approach, and evaluation criteria.
extended_description: These processes determine the engagement interactions with potential parties, the timing of the process, bring together the commercial and functional requirements into the tender documentation, the analysis and scoring mechanisms for tender analysis based on the functional, technical, operational and commercial requirements.

name: Administer the Tender Process
brief_description: Administer tender activities, including team engagement and evaluation of sourcing outcomes.
extended_description:
These processes manage the tender analysis team engagement approach.
These processes are invoked by the Party Order Handling processes in the event that the order process requires a tender to select between previously contracted parties.
These processes also manage the analysis of the strategic sourcing factors used at the commencement of the process including the industry and competitive analysis, and a determination of the minimum acceptable outcomes from the sourcing process.

name: Gain Tender Decision Approval
brief_description: Capture all activities required to develop and gain necessary approval for investment proposals to develop and deliver the required resource capabilities.
extended_description:
The Gain Tender Decision Approval processes capture all activities required to provide management oversight on the tender process and gain approval for the sourcing decision and party selection. These processes cover the establishment of any tender selection boards, the reporting processes and timetables, and the final approval of the tender decisions.
The processes include any interaction with cross-enterprise coordination and management functions to ensure that the tender decisions are supported by all stakeholders

name: Provide Management Oversight on Tenders
brief_description: These processes capture all activities required to provide management oversight on the tender process. These processes cover the establishment of any tender selection boards, the reporting processes and timetables

name: Approve Tender Decisions
brief_description: These processes capture all activities required to gain approval for the sourcing decision and party selection, including final approval of the tender decisions.

name: Party Relationship Development & Retirement
brief_description: Manage the lifecycles of parties with whom the enterprise has a relationship. Relationship with new parties may be required to broaden the services an enterprise offers, to improve performance, for outsourcing and out-tasking requirements, and so forth.
extended_description:
Party Relationship Development & Retirement manages the lifecycles of parties with whom the enterprise has a relationship. Relationship with new parties may be required to broaden the services an enterprise offers, to improve performance, for outsourcing and out-tasking requirements, and so forth.

Included processes that manage the Party's lifecycle, such as establishing and terminating a relationship, demographic collection, profiling, and community involvement.

name: Party Relationship Management
brief_description: Support the lifecycles (development and retirement) of an enterprise's relationships with parties.
extended_description:
Party Relationship Management manages the lifecycles of an enterprise's relationships with parties. A relationship with new parties may be required to broaden the services a service provider offers, to improve performance, for outsourcing and out-tasking requirements, and so forth.

These processes also manage the termination and re-establishment of a relationship with other parties, as well as evaluating the viability of continuing the relationship with the Party according to Party agreements.

name: Establish Party Relationship
brief_description: Verify the Party identity and manage a Party's identity across the enterprise.
extended_description: Establish Party Relationship verifies that a Party is who they claim they are to ensure only one Party identity exists across an enterprise, which can be referenced across the whole enterprise and allows the Party to quickly and easily identify itself, to establish and verify the Identity and to issue a unique Identifier and authentication information. Before establishing an identity for a new Party it is essential to check that it does not already have an Identity with the Enterprise.

name: Manage Party Relationship
brief_description: Establish and manage the on-going processes to support the commercial, strategic, delivery and operational interactions between an enterprise and Party.
extended_description:
Manage Party Relationship establishes and manages the on-going processes to support the commercial, strategic, delivery and operational interactions between the enterprise and a Party. It monitors, reviews, and agrees on changes to the commercial, strategic and operational interaction processes to improve their effectiveness.
This process oversees and administers any agreed joint management and/or process improvement activities between an enterprise and a Party. These joint activities could include operations monitoring and management, project related build and implementation activities, joint strategic management meetings, etc.

name: Monitor Party Relationship
brief_description: Monitor changes to the commercial, strategic and operational interaction processes.

name: Review Party Relationship
brief_description: Review changes to the commercial, strategic and operational interaction processes.

name: Approve Party Relationship
brief_description: Approve changes to the commercial, strategic and operational interaction processes.

name: Re-establish Party Relationship
brief_description: Re-establish Party Relationship re-establishes a relationship with a Party which was suspended or terminated in the past. It recovers the appropriate Party information along with past  interactions and provides them to the operational systems in order to provide continuity in the Party Relationship Management processes
extended_description: Re-establish Party Relationship re-establishes a relationship with a Party which was suspended or terminated in the past. It recovers the appropriate Party information along with past  interactions and provides them to the operational systems in order to provide continuity in the Party Relationship Management processes.

name: Terminate Party Relationship
brief_description: Manage the removal of a Party from an enterprise's value fabric.
extended_description:
Terminate Party Relationship manages the removal of a Party from an enterprise's value fabric, based on the continued inadequate performance based on monitoring and analysis performed by the Party Performance Management processes, and unsuccessful resolution through Manage Party Relationship Management processes.

A new Party may need to be found to replace the terminated Party. In this case the applicable processes, such as Identify Potential Parties, would be performed to accomplish this.

name: Collect Party Data
brief_description: Collect data about a Party and/or a Party playing a role.  Data includes basic Party data, identification data, contact data, and additional attributes.
extended_description: Collect Party Data collects data about a Party and/or a Party playing a role.  Data includes basic Party data, identification data, contact data, and additional attributes. This process also enables  modification and removal of Party data and Party role data and establishes the types of roles a Party can play.

name: Collect Basic Party Data
brief_description: Collect basic data about a Party, such as name, accounts and account contacts, credit profiles.
extended_description:
Collect Basic Party Data collects basic data about a Party, such as name, billing and bank accounts and account contacts (such as email and mobile number of the Party as well as other parties and their email and mobile number), credit profiles, and language ability. It also establishes relationships among Party accounts and Party roles.

It also establishes a type of role a Party can play as well as categorizations of roles.

name: Collect Party Identification
brief_description: Collect identification data about a Party (individual or organization), such as passport and company  (organization) registration.

name: Collect Party Contact
brief_description: Collect the medium in which a Party playing a role can be contacted, such as mobile phone and email.

name: Collect Party Skill
brief_description: Collect the skills possessed by a Party and/or a role played by a Party.

name: Collect Additional Party Attribute
brief_description: Collect additional attributes about a Party and/or a role a Party plays.
extended_description:
Collect Additional Party Attribute collects additional attributes about a Party and/or a role a Party plays. This is in addition to any other attributes collected for a Party or role a Party plays, including attributes collected by the Collect Party Data processes, and  Party and/or Party role demographics and profiles.  For example, for a Party playing the role of "lead" an attribute that defines how the lead found out about an enterprise may be defined.

This process also defines what attributes are to be collected for each type of Party/Party role.

name: Develop Party Relationship
brief_description: Provide an initial welcome to a Party, create an initial engagement plan, provide information useful to a Party's success, and provide training.
extended_description: Develop Party Relationship provides an initial welcome to the Party with whom a relationship has started. It creates an initial engagement plan which includes rules of engagement, initial plans for training, and describes the on-boarding process in more detail. Material is provided to a Party that they should find useful as their relationship with an enterprise continues to be developed, such as downloadable resources and brochures/datasheets/whitepapers. It also provide online and in person training, ongoing training on new solutions, new marketing strategies, and so forth.

name: Welcome New Party
brief_description: Provide an initial welcome to the Party with whom a relationship has started.
extended_description:
Welcome New Party provides an initial welcome to the Party with whom a relationship has started. The welcome may be communicated in a number of ways, such as a phone call, email, or visit to a Party.

A visit may be used if a Party is considered to be one in a top tier, such as a customer or partner who will contribute a significant amount of revenue to an enterprise. Scheduling, conducting, next steps, and evaluating a meeting are the responsibility of a appointment/calendaring process that would reside in Enterprise domain/Common Enterprise Processes; it has yet to be developed.

The communication would include:
-Executive & team introduction
-Access/explanation to the further on-boarding process
-Access to partner portal

The communication should provide the right level of detail to get the new Party started without being overwhelming.

name: Develop Party Relationship Success Business Plan
brief_description: Create an initial engagement plan which includes rules of engagement, initial plans for training, and describes the on-boarding process in more detail.
extended_description: Develop Party Relationship Success Business Plan creates an initial engagement plan which includes rules of engagement, initial plans for training, describes on-boarding processes in more detail such as profile, demographic. For partners it further describes Party or enterprise product offering on-boarding and agrees to marketing activities. It also defines how an enterprise and a Party will both measure success.

name: Enable Party
brief_description: Provide material to a Party that they should find useful as their relationship with an enterprise continues to be developed, such as downloadable resources and brochures/datasheets/whitepapers.
extended_description: Enable Party provides material to a Party that they should find useful as their relationship with an enterprise continues to be developed.  This includes, but is not limited to downloadable resources, brochures/datasheets/whitepapers, and product offering pricing information/configuration tools. For partners it includes messaging documents and competitive information.

name: Train Party
brief_description: Provide online and in person training, ongoing training on new solutions, new marketing strategies, and so forth.
extended_description:
Train Party provides online and in person training, ongoing training on new solutions, new marketing strategies, and so forth.

The Party Training & Education process is employed to develop any Party specific training and carry out the training.

name: Onboard Party Identity
brief_description: Onboard Party Identity creates a suitable identity for all parties, and ensure that the identity they carry is valid for the business purpose intended
extended_description:
Onboard Party Identity creates a suitable identity for all parties, and ensure that the identity they carry is valid for the business purpose intended
Note:
Enterprises need to be able to create a suitable identity for all parties they interact with.  Every organization's trust capital is based on their knowledge of parties they interact with.  If interactions are to be managed, the organization needs to be clear as to who other parties are, and ensure that the identity they carry is valid for the business purpose intended.  Authentication and assigning of privileges are key interactions between the organization and the Party, and are logged in for security control purpose.

name: Validate Party ID
brief_description: Validate party identity at the level required for the relevant business purpose.
extended_description:
Validate Party ID is responsible for confirming the identity of parties.
Note:
If an organization carries an identity of an interacting Party, the identity needs to be validated at a level suitable for the business purpose.  Some national jurisdictions require an explicit validation of subscriber identities by enterprises before specified services can be provided.  Most validation are, however at the discretion of the service provider.

name: Assign Privileges to Parties
brief_description: Assign party privileges that govern how parties may interact with the organization.
extended_description:
Assign Privileges to Parties is responsible to set the party's level of privileges.
Note:
 A parties' ability to interact with an organization is bounded by the privileges the organization assigns to the party.  While privileges are defined by strategy, policy and intent, they have a profound impact on the parties' experience of the organization, and thus need to be assigned with care.  Privileges are typically assigned to a parties identity, and are accessed from the context of that identity.

name: Authenticate Party Identity on Access
brief_description: Authenticate party identity when access is requested to protect the enterprise trust regime.
extended_description: Authenticate Party Identity on Access ensures identification upon access is corroborated . Authentication is key interaction with parties as they engage with an organization.  Effective authentication will deliver both an acceptable experience for the Party, and ensure that the enterprise trust regime is not compromised

name: Record Party Access in Tamper Proof Store
brief_description: Record party access events in a tamper-proof store to support trust, recall, and compliance.
extended_description: Party authentication is such a key interaction that a specific activity to ensure that the event is recorded in a tamper proof register.  Much of a Party's trust will hinge on both the ability to recall this event when disputed, and on the degree to which the log is believed to be tamperproof.  Some legal domains require this explicitly.

name: Party Demographic Collection
brief_description: Defines and collect demographic information about parties, such as their size, growth, density, and distribution, as well as statistics regarding birth, marriage, disease, and death.
extended_description:
Party Demographic Collection defines and collects demographic information about parties, such as their size, growth, density, and distribution, as well as statistics regarding birth, marriage, disease, and death.

Demographic data is information about parties that allows decisions to be made such as the make-up and size of a market segment, classification and ranking of customers, and so forth.  Demographics provide the key “what” information and can be broken down into two categories:  individual demographics and organization demographics.

name: Specify Party Demographic Definition
brief_description: Define a type of demographics to be collected about parties and/or a role a Party plays.
extended_description: Specify Party Demographic Definition defines a type of demographic to be collected about parties and/or a role a Party plays. This includes specifying the permitted values associated with a demographic, such as age ranges, income ranges, as well as associations to  market segments and so forth. This process also enables changes to be made to any of these aspects for a demographic's definition.

name: Specify Party Demographic Definition Group
brief_description: Group Party demographic definitions or define a group of groups.
extended_description:
Specify Party Demographic Definition Group defines a group Party demographic definitions or defines a group of groups.  For example for an organization a group may represent a collection of demographics about the organization itself, such as headquarters location, number and location of offices (domestic vs. international, regions/triads);  each have different access requirements.

This process also enables changes  and deletions to be made to any grouping.

name: Remove Party Demographic Definition
brief_description: Remove a Party demographic definition, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.
extended_description: Remove Party Demographic  Definition removes a Party demographic definition, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.  Care must be taken when deleting a demographic definition, because any Party demographics related to it may also be deleted or could lose their context.  Often the choice is to mark the demographic as no longer valid to preclude collecting it for any more parties.

name: Collect Party Demographic
brief_description: Collect a demographic about a Party and/or one or more roles a Party plays.
extended_description:
Collect Party Demographic collects a demographic about a Party and/or one or more roles a Party plays. The demographic is placed in a group according to the definition of the demographic.  Its relationship to a geographic area, product offering, or market segment may also be established.

It can be collected directly from a Party or from another source, such as social media, professional groups to which a Party belongs, and census data.

This process also enables changes to be made to any of these aspects for a demographic.

name: Remove Party Demographic
brief_description: Remove a Party demographic, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.
extended_description: Remove Party Demographic removes a Party demographic, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.  For example, a Party privacy agreement may specify that a certain fact about a part be removed via deletion after an agreed upon period of time; this is typically referred to "as the right to be forgotten".

name: Party Profiling
brief_description: Define and collect attributes that are used to create and maintain Party profiles or  profiles for a role played by a Party.  These attributes are in addition to basic information maintained about a Party, such as name, identification,  contact information, and demographics.
extended_description:
Party Profiling defines and collects attributes that are used to create and maintain Party profiles or  profiles for a role played by a Party.  These attributes are in addition to basic information maintained about a Party, such as name, identification, contact information, and demographics. Profile attributes may include product offering preferences, social media memberships, and so forth.

Party profiles can be used in a number of ways including targeting parties for marketing campaigns and/or product offerings and classifying parties into market segments.

name: Define Party Profile Type
brief_description: Define a type of Party profile and its attributes to be collected about parties and/or a role a Party plays.
extended_description:
Define Party Profile Type defines a type of Party profile and its attributes to be collected about parties and/or a role a Party plays. This includes specifying the permitted values associated with a  Party profile attribute, such as interests/hobbies, education, product offering preferences.  Demographic information can also be linked to a Party profile type's attributes. This process also enables changes to be made to any of these aspects for a demographics' definition.

This process may also relate a Party profile type to a market segment for grouping parties into segments or to marketing  campaigns and product offerings to target parties for them.

name: Define Party Profile Type Attribute Group
brief_description: Group Party  profile type attributes or define a group of groups.
extended_description:
Define Party Profile Type Attribute Group defines a group Party profile attributes   or defines a group of groups.  For example for an individual a group may represent a collection of educational information or interests and hobbies.

This process also enables changes  and deletions to be made to any grouping.

name: Remove Party Profile Type
brief_description: Remove a Party  profile type and/or one or more of its attributes, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.
extended_description: Remove Party Profile Type removes a Party profile type and/or one or more of its attributes, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.  Care must be taken when deleting a profile type and/or one or more of its attributes, because any Party profiles or Party profile attribute(s) related to them may also be deleted or could lose their context.  Often the choice is to mark the profile type and/or attribute(s) as no longer valid to preclude collecting it for any more parties.

name: Collect Party Profile
brief_description: Create a profile for a Party and/or a Party role and collect profile attribute values. For example, a list of hobbies in which a Party is involved.
extended_description:
Collect Party Profile creates a profile for a Party and/or a Party role and collects profile attribute values. For example, a list of hobbies in which a Party is involved. The attribute is placed in a group if it is defined as part of one. Demographics about the Party may become part of the profile if a relationship between the two has been specified.

It can be collected directly from a Party or from another source, such as social media or professional groups to which a Party belongs,.

This process also enables changes to be made to any of these aspects for a profile or a profile's attribute(s).

name: Remove Party Profile
brief_description: Remove a Party profile and/or one or more profile attributes, either by deleting it or indicating it is no longer valid.

name: Business Partner Offering Development & Retirement
brief_description: Manage on-boarding and off-boarding another Business Partner's product specifications and product offerings that a required to facilitate the business model of the enterprise.
extended_description:
Business Partner Offering Development & Retirement supports the management of on-boarding and off-boarding another Business Partner's product specifications and product offerings that a required to facilitate the business model of the enterprise.

It also manages the involvement the enterprise has with a product specification and product offering. For example, the enterprise may accept an order for one of its offerings, but it may be fulfilled by another Business Partner.

Note:
- Product Specification Development & Retirement and Product Offering Development & Retirement processes are used to manage most of the lifecycle of product specifications and product offerings. This is done to eliminate redundant processes.  For example, the Product Offering Pricing processes are used to manage the prices associated with on-boarded product offerings.
- This process therefore focuses on managing the relationship that parties, including the enterprise, have with product specifications and product offerings as well as the impact of off-boarding specifications and offerings on a provider's service and resource infrastructure.

name: On-board Business Partner Product Specification & Offering
brief_description:
Manages the on-boarding another Business Partner's product offering or a product specification upon which the offering is based.

Also manage the involvement the enterprise has with a product specification and offering.
extended_description:
On-board Business Partner Product Specification & Offering manages the on-boarding another Business Partner's product offering or a product specification upon which the offering is based.

It also manages the involvement the enterprise has with a Business Partner's product specification and offering. For example, the enterprise may accept an order for one of its offerings, but it may be fulfilled by another Business Partner.

By using the on-boarded specifications, this process allows the enterprise to create new product offerings that leverage its own product offerings as well as the acquired product offerings. It may also make a Business Partner's offerings available as-is to the market.

The specifications for the product offering made available by another Business Partner in  catalog may be from a wholesaler’s perspective, while the specification in the enterprise’s catalog may be from a retailer’s perspective, therefore this process maintains the relationship between the enterprise's product specification and product offering and those provided by another Business Partner.

It is also used to modify the involvement associated with a Business Partner's, including the enterprise, product specifications or offerings. For example, if the Business Partner who accept payments for a purchased product offering changes.

This process is initially invoked during and after the agreement for a particular product specification and/or product offering has been established and approved. It is also invoked when modifications to the product specifications or offerings are implemented by another Business Partner in accordance with the terms and conditions and the process to manage the variance of an agreement.

name: Define Business Partner Product Specification Involvement
brief_description: On-board a product specification from another Business Partner's catalog.  Also manage the enterprise's relationship with a product specification.
extended_description:
Define Business Partner Product Specification Involvement  on-boards a product specification from another Business Partner's catalog  It also manages the enterprise's relationship with a product specification. It also manages the relationships between an enterprises product specification and that of another Business Partner. It also manages Product Specification Tests proposed by the enterprise.  Until an on-boarding agreement is approved the product specification is marked as tentatively on-boarded. Once the agreement is approved the specification is marked as on-boarded.

By using the on-boarded specifications, this process allows the enterprise to create new product offerings that leverage its own product offering as well as another Business Partner's offering.

The specifications for the product offering made available by another Business Partner  may be from a wholesaler’s perspective, while the enterprise's specification may be from a retailer’s perspective. Therefore this process also maintains the relationship between the enterprise's product specification and one provided by another Business Partner.

It is also used to modify the involvement associated with a Business Partner's, including the enterprise, product specifications"

name: Define Business Partner Product Offering Involvement
brief_description: On-board a product offering from the another Business Partner's catalog to the enterprise’s inventory of product offerings and its catalogs.
extended_description:
Define Business Partner Product Offering Involvement on-boards a product offering from the another Business Partner's catalog to the enterprise’s inventory of product offerings and its catalogs.  It also manages the relationships between an enterprises product offering and that of another Business Partner; for example a relationship that indicates an enterprises orders an offering from another Business Partner. Until an on-boarding agreement is approved the product offering is marked as tentatively on-boarded. Once the agreement is approved the offering is marked as on-boarded.

It defines the involvement from a process perspective that a Business Partner, including the enterprise, has with its offering.  For example, if a Business Partner takes an order, fulfills it after taking the order, accepts payment, receives payment, after sales service provided for the offering after it is acquired, and so forth.

It also manages the enterprise's relationship with a product offering and its relationship with those provided by another Business Partner. For example, an enterprise may make an offering available on behalf of another Business Partner or acquire an offering for re-sale from another Business Partner.

It is also used to modify the involvement associated with a Business Partner's, including the enterprise, product offerings. For example, if the Business Partner who accept payments for a purchased product offering changes.

name: Off-Board Business Partner Offering & Specification
brief_description: Off-board a Business Partner's offering or specification.  If a specification is off-boarded all associated offerings are off-boarded. This can occur when the agreement for a product specification and/or offering is terminated. If an agreement covers multiple specifications and/or offerings off-boarding is done for the item on an agreement that is terminated.
extended_description:
Off-Board Business Partner Offering & Specification off-boards a Business Partner's offering or specification.  If a specification is off-boarded all associated offerings are off-boarded. This can occur when the agreement for a product specification  and/or offering is terminated. If an agreement covers multiple specifications and/or offerings off-boarding is done for the item on an agreement that is terminated. When the final product offering related to a product specification is off-boarded the product specification may also be off-boarded.

If a product specification is off-boarded then disposition of related service specifications, services, resource specifications, and/or resources is made.

The  off-boarding by the enterprise of the capabilities is gradual and allows enough time to account for any contractual obligations of the enterprise with its customers, but without violating the terms and conditions of any agreement with the Business Partner.

name: Off-Board Business Partner Product Offering
brief_description: Off-board a Business Partner's product offering. This can occur when an agreement or an item on an agreement associated with a product offering is terminated.
extended_description:
Off-Board Business Partner Product Offering off-boards a Business Partner's product offering. This can occur when an agreement or an item on an agreement associated with a product offering is terminated.

When the final product offering related to a product specification is off-boarded the product specification may also be off-boarded by the Off-Board Business Partner Product Specification process.

Note that this process will interact with the Manage Product Offering Exit process which is part of Product Offering Development & Retirement.

name: Off-Board Business Partner Product Specification
brief_description:
Off-board a Business Partner's product specification.
This can occur when the agreement for this product specification is terminated or an item on an agreement associated with the specification for this product offering is terminated.
extended_description:
Off-Board Business Partner Product Specification off-boards a Business Partner's product specification and related product specification tests. This can occur when the agreement for this product specification is terminated or an item on an agreement associated with the specification for this product offering is terminated.

When a product specification is off-boarded then disposition of related service specifications, services, resource specifications, and/or resources is made.

The off-boarding of the specifications and retirement of the product specification by the enterprise is gradual.  This allows enough time to account for any contractual obligations of the enterprise with its customers, but without violating the terms and conditions of agreements with the Business Partner.

name: Remove Business Partner Product Specification
brief_description: Remove a Business Partner's product specification.
extended_description:
Remove Business Partner Product Specification removes a Business Partner's product specification and related product specification testing .
This can occur when the agreement for this product specification is terminated or an item on an agreement associated with the specification for this product offering is terminated.

Note that this process will interact with the Remove Product Specification Exit process which is part of Product Specification Development & Retirement.

name: De-activate Off-boarded Preconfigured Services
brief_description: Deactivate any services have been pre-configured for the associated party's product specification.  This is accomplished by notifying the  Service Configuration & Activation to de-activate them.
extended_description: De-activate Off-boarded Preconfigured Services deactivates any services have been pre-configured for the associated party's product specification.  This is accomplished by notifying the  Service Configuration & Activation to de-activate them. If the deactivated services are the final ones associated with a service specification the Manage Service Exit process is notified for possible removal of the service specification.

name: Return Remaining Off-boarded Product (Resource) Inventory
